report.summary: Chunk 1 of artifacts.py: module docstring defining the DATA layer, three tiers, invariants; constants and helper functions for artifact identification.
risks: artifact_node_id | low | Uses PurePosixPath normalization but not pathlib.Path.resolve; may produce IDs that differ from actual file paths. | Add a test with relative and absolute paths.

handoff.purpose: Define module constants, artifact kind mapping, and helper functions for artifact identification.

claims.text: The type layer describes shapes declared in code — what a function says it takes and returns. This layer describes artefacts that move between programs — which file a script reads, which it writes, and what schema that file actually carries.
claims.why: Claims about the type layer and its separation are not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: In a physics analysis those are genuinely two worlds: analysis.cpp --writes--> selected.root (TTree "events": voltage/Float_t …) plot_eff.py --reads---> selected.root --writes--> fig/eff_vs_v.pdf paper.tex --figures-> fig/eff_vs_v.pdf "the efficiency is 98.2%"
claims.why: The example is illustrative; no code in this chunk implements or verifies this chain.

claims.text: Nobody can follow that chain today, because every link is a convention — a path spelled inside a string literal — rather than a declaration, and every hop crosses a language boundary.
claims.why: Assertion about current tools; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: A path literal, however, is a path literal in LaTeX, C++, Python, Fortran, Verilog and a Makefile alike, which is why this layer generalises where the type layer cannot.
claims.why: Claim about generalization; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: An edge alone says "this script touches that file". The interesting question is whether the schema the code declares and the schema the file carries agree.
claims.why: Claim about purpose; no schema comparison code in this chunk.

claims.text: A renamed branch, a changed unit, a column that quietly moved — those are the defects that survive every test suite and then appear in a thesis.
claims.why: Anecdotal; not verifiable.

claims.text: So this module extracts artefact schemas as first-class data (ArtifactSchema) and offers compare_schema so a later lane can report the DISAGREEMENT, which is the finding worth acting on.
claims.why: ArtifactSchema and compare_schema are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: tier 0 path literals -> artefact edges. No file is opened. Works for every language with a pattern below.
claims.why: Tier 0 implementation not present in this chunk.

claims.text: tier 1 schema as DECLARED IN CODE (TTree::Branch("voltage", …), read_csv(names=[…])). Not implemented here yet; the hook is SCHEMA_FROM_CODE and it reports not_supported until it exists.
claims.why: SCHEMA_FROM_CODE not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: tier 2 schema read FROM THE ARTEFACT. Implemented with stdlib only for CSV, JSON and NPY.
claims.why: Tier 2 readers not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ROOT/HDF5/Parquet need optional readers (uproot, h5py, pyarrow); absent, they report not_supported — never an empty schema, because "we could not look" and "there are no columns" must not render the same.
claims.why: Readers not present; claim about behavior not verifiable.

claims.text: Refuse to guess. A literal that does not resolve to a file present in the file set is DROPPED and COUNTED, never bound to a near-match.
claims.why: No literal resolution logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Same rule markdown.py applies to document links.
claims.why: Reference to another file not present.

claims.text: A literal matching more than one candidate is AMBIGUOUS and produces no edge.
claims.why: No disambiguation logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Metadata only, never the payload. A .root file is gigabytes; its branch list is kilobytes. Schema reads are bounded by MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES and stop at the header. This layer never ingests data.
claims.why: MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES is defined as 256*1024; the claim about bounded reads is consistent with the constant. No data ingestion code is present.

claims.text: Reading is not executing. No file here is imported, run, or evaluated.
claims.why: No file reading code in this chunk.

claims.text: But parsing a hostile binary is still an attack surface, so every reader is bounded and failure is reported as unreadable, never as an empty schema.
claims.why: No reader implementation in this chunk.

claims.text: Artefacts are not code. Artefact nodes get their own id namespace and never enter modules, import_edges, all_units or the symbol resolver — the same carve-out the type layer publishes in excluded_from.
claims.why: artifact_node_id produces IDs with 'artifact:' prefix; is_artifact_node_id checks for that prefix. The separation is enforced by the naming convention.

claims.text: The artefact family for a path, or None if it is not an artefact.
claims.why: Function returns kind[0] if suffix matches ARTIFACT_KINDS, else None.

claims.text: Own namespace. Must be impossible to mistake for a module rel path — the type layer learned the same lesson with type:/field:.
claims.why: Returns string starting with 'artifact:'.

observations.what: Docstring claims about tier 0, tier 1, tier 2, and invariants are largely uncheckable because the actual implementation is not in this chunk.
artifact_family uses PurePosixPath(rel.replace('\\','/')).suffix.lower() which normalizes backslashes; this is consistent with artifact_node_id which also replaces backslash with forward slash.
The constants MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES, MAX_COLUMNS, MAX_LITERALS_PER_FILE are defined but not used in this chunk; their enforcement is elsewhere.
ARTIFACT_KINDS includes '.npy' as having a reader (True) but '.npz' as False; the docstring claims NPY is supported but not NPZ.
